title: Launch scrimmage + backstop cadence (Nov 2027) - sketch
summary: Compact pre-launch scrimmage plan with staffing cadences, backstop triggers, and a concise draft of release notes for the feature wave scheduled in early Nov 2027.
body:
Purpose:
Quick, tactical runbook used for the 72-hour window around the Nov release. This doc is intentionally compact — it's a rehearsal + backstop cadence to be used by the launch crew and the night-watch team.

Goals:
- Validate staffing handovers and communication loops during a preflight scrimmage on Nov 02-03.
- Confirm fallback (backstop) policies for model routing, capacity, and API degradations.
- Produce a short, consumer-facing release notes draft and an internal postmortem checklist template.

Key dates (local PT):
- 2027-11-01 09:00 — Preflight sync: owners + SRE + product (30m)
- 2027-11-02 14:00 — Scrimmage start: run a simulated traffic spike and failover test (2h)
- 2027-11-02 17:00 — Post-scrimmage retro + quick fixes (60m)
- 2027-11-03 22:00 — Go/no-go poll (if still on schedule)
- 2027-11-04 00:00 — Blackout window begins (no non-critical deploys)
- 2027-11-04 02:00 — Target gradual traffic ramp to new variant (if go)

Compact preflight checklist (scrimmage focus):
- Telemetry: verify alert thresholds for 95th/99th latency, 5xx spike, and queue length.
- Canary slots: ensure canary nodes reserved and health-checks return green.
- KV cache warmup: run prefix-warm script against canary with synthetic prompts.
- Autoscaler: smoke test scale-up policy with synthetic load generator.
- Model artifacts: checksum & version pinned in deployment manifest.
- Secrets & KMS: confirm rotation window is closed and keys accessible.
- Rollback toggle: create quick rollback switch in Console and validate it flips route in < 45s.
- Communication: #launch-run channel created, runbook link pinned, incident playbook attached.

Scrimmage runbook outline (roles + immediate play):
- Conductor (Marin): coordinate timeline, run go/no-go poll, call interrupts.
- SRE lead (Dana): monitor infra, own autoscaler, run vertical scaling patches.
- Model lead (Priya): verify model variant integrity, monitor perf regressions.
- Platform eng (Tom): execute canary push and handle rollback switch.
- Support liaison (Ethan): triage customer tickets, hold standby CS responders.

Observed failure scenarios to exercise:
- Canary health failure: automated revert to previous routing; verify KV consistency after revert.
- Latency tail spike: trigger fallback to lower-cost, lower-latency model variant.
- Throttling surge: validate token-limited shedding behavior and SLO reporting.
- Partial network partition (region): confirm smart routing to alternate region and telemetry labeling.

Backstop policies (operational knobs and thresholds):
- Latency guard: if p99 > 1200ms for 3 consecutive minutes, reduce canary traffic by 50% and notify SRE.
- Error guard: if 5xx rate > 0.8% sustained for 2 minutes, full rollback (route to previous stable).
- Cost throttle: if burst unit cost > 2.5x baseline for 5m, divert to cheaper variant and flag finance.
- Region failover: if region loss > 30% of capacity or sustained 5xx > 1% for 5m, migrate 100% traffic to fallback region.

Release notes draft (consumer-facing — short):
- New: improved response correctness for instruction-following prompts (model variant r1.3).
- Improved: 15% median latency reduction for chat endpoints in EU regions.
- Fixed: rare 502s caused by connection churn during autoscaling events.
- Known issue: short-lived tokenization warning may appear for very long single-turn prompts — harmless; will be removed in next patch.

Internal release notes (engineering bullets):
- Model pinned: r1.3 (sha256: abcdef1234) behind canary; fallback to r1.2 if rollback.
- Config changes: batching window increased to 25ms for chat-prod route.
- Infra tweak: autoscaler cooldown reduced from 120s to 45s for canary pool.

Post-release immediate tasks (0-24h):
- Telemetry deep-dive: collect sample traces for any p95+ anomalies.
- Ticket triage: support to escalate customer-impacting errors to Sev2+ Slack channel.
- Canary retention: keep canary traffic at 10% for 6 hours before continuing ramp.
- Postmortem stub: owner to draft initial timeline within 12h of any Sev1/Sev2.

24-72h stabilization checklist:
- Monitor quality metrics (eval prompt set) and open dedicated regression tickets if MRR drop > 2%.
- Reconcile costs vs estimate and report to finance by day+3.
- Run a small synthetic long-sequence workload overnight to validate KV cache behavior.

Open questions & run decisions (to be resolved during preflight):
- Do we enable aggressive batching for EU during the ramp or keep baseline? (product + infra decision)
- Are we comfortable with the new autoscaler cooldown parameter for peak traffic? (SRE signoff needed)
- Temporary CS messaging: who drafts the short public note if we experience a partial degradation?

Appendix: quick links and artifacts
- Synthetic load tool: github.com/redwood/load-tools spike-runner --profile release-test
- Rollout toggle: Console > Releases > active > release-2027-11 > toggle
- Incident playbook: confluence:incident-handbook#runbooks/latency

Notes to reviewers:
- This is intentionally terse and operational. Use the scrimmage window to run the scenarios that feel most risky for your teams. Add any missing quick commands or pager steps directly in the #launch-run channel pinned message.

Change log for this doc:
- 2027-10-20 Marin: initial sketch and timeline
- 2027-10-25 Priya: added model fallback thresholds
- 2027-11-02 Dana: updated scrimmage start time and staff assignments after calendar sync
